question: Why can Rudra-descents differ even when they share the same basic status?
premises: Even when the state of being a Rudra-descent is the same, action and experience can differ.
Any embodied form of a being is interwoven with many powers.
The configuration of those powers makes each embodied form distinct.
inference: Rudra-descents vary because each embodied manifestation is shaped by a distinct configuration of powers, karma, and experience.
uncertainties: The scope of 'being' here may include both divine descents and embodied entities more generally.
plain_english: Even when two cases are both descents of Rudra, their karma and experience can differ. That is because whatever body a being takes is woven together from many powers.
